<file path="prisma/schema.prisma">
// ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════
// 🛒 shop/ — Prisma schema
// ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════
// Phase 1 ships ONLY the generator + datasource.
// All models (User, Product, Order, etc.) land in Phase 2.
//
// Deployment notes (from the Lumière lessons):
//   • prisma-client-js — NOT the newer `prisma-client` generator.
//     Outputs to node_modules and is bundled correctly on Vercel.
//   • binaryTargets — native (dev) + rhel-openssl-3.0.x (Vercel).
//   • DATABASE_URL is the runtime connection (direct endpoint on Neon).
//   • DIRECT_URL is used only by `prisma migrate`.

generator client {
  provider      = "prisma-client-js"
  binaryTargets = ["native", "rhel-openssl-3.0.x"]
}

datasource db {
  provider  = "postgresql"
  url       = env("DATABASE_URL")
  directUrl = env("DIRECT_URL")
}
</file>

    <header class="hero">
      <div class="kicker">Phase 01 · Audit &amp; Scaffolding</div>
      <h1>Legacy Audit &amp; the shop/ Foundation</h1>
      <p class="lede">Verify every bug in the legacy MERN storefront against the real source code, then establish a clean Next.js 16 + Prisma 6 + Neon scaffold in a sibling <code>shop/</code> folder. The legacy <code>front/</code>, <code>admin/</code>, <code>back/</code> trees remain untouched as reference — the new app is a separate git repository.</p>
      <div class="stack">
        <span>Legacy Audit</span><span>16+ Bugs</span><span>Next.js 16</span>
        <span>Prisma 6</span><span>Neon</span><span>Webpack</span>
        <span>Husky · Prettier · ESLint</span>
      </div>
    </header>

    <section id="overview">
      <h2><span class="num">1</span> Overview</h2>
      <p><strong>Goal.</strong> Before writing a single line of new code, prove every claim in the bug inventory against the actual source files. Then stand up <code>shop/</code> with the same production patterns proven in the earlier Lumière project — no regressions, no re-litigating decisions.</p>
      <h3>Deliverables</h3>
      <ol>
        <li>A verified bug table — every inventory item, checked against the source, with file:line evidence.</li>
        <li>A second look for bugs the original audit missed.</li>
        <li>A scaffolded <code>shop/</code>: Next.js 16, TypeScript, Tailwind 4, Prisma 6, ESLint, Prettier, Husky.</li>
        <li>Working <code>prisma validate</code> and <code>prisma generate</code> against a Neon connection.</li>
        <li>A green <code>npm run build</code> with <code>PrismaPlugin</code> active.</li>
        <li>The Lumière deployment gotchas baked in from day one — <code>prisma-client-js</code>, <code>binaryTargets</code>, <code>--webpack</code>, direct Neon endpoint.</li>
      </ol>
    </section>

    <section id="strategy">
      <h2><span class="num">2</span> Audit Strategy</h2>
      <p>The legacy codebase is 40+ files across three Vite/CRA-style apps. Every bug listed in the brief was re-read against the actual source — no assumptions, no <em>“probably still true.”</em> Where the brief's summary was imprecise, I corrected it in the table.</p>
      <div class="callout info">
        <strong>Rule followed</strong>
        If the audit disagrees with the brief, the audit wins — and the difference is documented. Fixing a bug that was already fixed would be wasted work; missing one that's still live would be worse.
      </div>
      <p>The inventory was split into four categories:</p>
      <table>
        <thead><tr><th>Category</th><th>Count</th><th>Meaning</th></tr></thead>
        <tbody>
          <tr><td><span class="badge crit">CRITICAL</span></td><td>3</td><td>Page crash or guaranteed dead UI</td></tr>
          <tr><td><span class="badge sec">SECURITY</span></td><td>4</td><td>Authentication bypass, credential leak, path traversal</td></tr>
          <tr><td><span class="badge log">LOGIC</span></td><td>9</td><td>Silent state desync, missing validation, missing webhook</td></tr>
          <tr><td><span class="badge data">DATA</span></td><td>2</td><td>Extra findings from the audit pass</td></tr>
        </tbody>
      </table>
    </section>

    <section id="critical">
      <h2><span class="num">3</span> CRITICAL Bugs — Verified</h2>

      <h3>#1 — <code>all_products</code> imported from a commented-out export</h3>
      <table>
        <thead><tr><th>File</th><th>Evidence</th></tr></thead>
        <tbody>
          <tr><td><code>front/src/assets/data.js</code></td><td>The export block is entirely commented out starting at the banner <code>// export const all_products = [...]</code>. Only <code>categories</code> is live.</td></tr>
          <tr><td><code>front/src/components/Categories.jsx</code></td><td><code>import { categories, all_products } from "../assets/data"</code> — the second name is undefined at runtime.</td></tr>
          <tr><td><code>front/src/components/Offer.jsx</code></td><td>Same import. Then <code>all_products.slice(0, 12)</code> — a TypeError on load.</td></tr>
        </tbody>
      </table>
      <p><strong>Verdict:</strong> confirmed live. Both routes crash with <code>Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'slice')</code>.</p>
      <div class="callout danger">
        <strong>Root cause</strong>
        Two sources of truth — the API in <code>ShopContext</code> and the static <code>data.js</code> — were patched at different times. Deleting the static source without updating its consumers broke them silently.
      </div>

      <h3>#2 — Admin order list always empty</h3>
      <table>
        <thead><tr><th>Side</th><th>Code</th></tr></thead>
        <tbody>
          <tr><td>Frontend reads</td><td><code>admin/src/components/Orders.jsx</code> → <code>setOrders(res.data.orders.reverse())</code></td></tr>
          <tr><td>Backend returns</td><td><code>back/controllers/orderController.js</code> → <code>res.json({ success: true, data: orders })</code></td></tr>
        </tbody>
      </table>
      <p><strong>Verdict:</strong> confirmed. <code>res.data.orders</code> is <code>undefined</code> → <code>.reverse()</code> throws inside the try/catch, the catch logs and swallows, and the UI is left empty with a red toast.</p>

      <h3>#3 — Three placeholder components shipping dead code</h3>
      <table>
        <thead><tr><th>File</th><th>Body</th></tr></thead>
        <tbody>
          <tr><td><code>front/src/components/Navbar.jsx</code></td><td><code>return &lt;div&gt;Navbar&lt;/div&gt;</code></td></tr>
          <tr><td><code>front/src/components/Item.jsx</code></td><td><code>return &lt;div&gt;Item&lt;/div&gt;</code></td></tr>
          <tr><td><code>front/src/components/ProductDisplay.jsx</code></td><td><code>return &lt;div&gt;ProductDisplay&lt;/div&gt;</code></td></tr>
        </tbody>
      </table>
      <p><strong>Verdict:</strong> confirmed. All three are <code>memo()</code>-wrapped single-line stubs. Nothing imports them — they exist as dead code. Decision recorded in Phase 4: <strong>delete</strong>, don't implement. Their intended responsibilities are already covered by <code>Header.jsx</code>, <code>Categories.jsx</code>, and <code>Product.jsx</code>.</p>
    </section>

    <section id="security">
      <h2><span class="num">4</span> SECURITY Bugs — Verified</h2>

      <h3>#4 — Admin login bypasses the backend entirely</h3>
      <pre><code>// admin/src/components/AdminLogin.jsx
if (formData.email === "admin@gmail.com" &&
    formData.password === "123456") {
  localStorage.setItem("admin", "true");
  navigate("/admin/add");
}</code></pre>
      <p><strong>Verdict:</strong> confirmed. Any visitor reading the bundled JS sees the credentials. The backend <code>adminLogin</code> controller exists but is never called.</p>

      <h3>#5 — ProtectedRoute checks a key nothing writes</h3>
      <pre><code>// admin/src/components/ProtectedRoute.jsx
const token = localStorage.getItem("adminToken");
if (!token) return &lt;Navigate to="/admin/login" replace /&gt;;</code></pre>
      <p><strong>Verdict:</strong> confirmed. A repo-wide grep for <code>setItem("adminToken"</code> returns nothing in <code>admin/src/</code>. Login stores <code>"admin"</code>, not <code>"adminToken"</code>. The proper flow is unreachable.</p>

      <h3>#6 — Public <code>setupFirstAdmin</code> endpoint</h3>
      <pre><code>// back/routes/adminRoutes.js
adminRouter.post("/setup", setupFirstAdmin);  // no middleware

// back/controllers/adminController.js
const existingAdmin = await userModel.findOne({ isAdmin: true });
if (existingAdmin) return res.json({ success: false, ... });
// ...else create a new admin with attacker-supplied credentials</code></pre>
      <p><strong>Verdict:</strong> confirmed. On a fresh database, the first caller to hit <code>POST /api/admin/setup</code> becomes the admin. The endpoint never gets deleted because the developer forgets.</p>

      <h3>#7 — Committed <code>.env</code> files, including Stripe keys</h3>
      <table>
        <thead><tr><th>File</th><th>Committed secret</th></tr></thead>
        <tbody>
          <tr><td><code>back/.env</code></td><td><code>MONGO_URL</code>, <code>JWT_SECRET</code>, <code>STRIPE_SECRET_KEY</code></td></tr>
          <tr><td><code>front/.env</code></td><td><code>VITE_STRIPE_PK</code> (publishable — lower risk, but still)</td></tr>
          <tr><td><code>admin/.env</code></td><td><code>VITE_API_URL</code> (harmless)</td></tr>
        </tbody>
      </table>
      <p>Both <code>.gitignore</code> files contain <code>*.local</code> but <strong>not</strong> <code>.env</code>. Confirmed by direct inspection of the <code>.gitignore</code> contents.</p>
      <div class="callout danger">
        <strong>Phase 10 action item</strong>
        Rotate the legacy <code>JWT_SECRET</code> and <code>STRIPE_SECRET_KEY</code> even though <code>shop/</code> is a fresh repo — the old keys remain in the legacy git history and are public if that repository is ever pushed.
      </div>

      <h3>#14 — Multer accepts anything, no filename sanitization</h3>
      <pre><code>// back/routes/productRoutes.js
const storage = multer.diskStorage({
  destination: "uploads",
  filename: (req, file, cb) =>
    cb(null, `${Date.now()}-${file.originalname}`),
});
const upload = multer({ storage });  // no fileFilter, no limits</code></pre>
      <p><strong>Verdict:</strong> confirmed. No <code>fileFilter</code> (accepts <code>.exe</code>, <code>.html</code>, <code>.svg</code> — stored as-is, served back from <code>/images/*</code>). No <code>limits</code> (unbounded size). The filename is trusted verbatim — a crafted <code>originalname</code> like <code>..%2F..%2Fetc%2Fpasswd</code> can escape the <code>uploads/</code> directory depending on OS behavior.</p>
    </section>

    <section id="logic">
      <h2><span class="num">5</span> LOGIC Bugs — Verified</h2>

      <h3>#8 — Two sources of truth for products</h3>
      <p><code>ShopContext.jsx</code> fetches from <code>/api/product/list</code> on mount. But <code>Categories.jsx</code> and <code>Offer.jsx</code> import <code>all_products</code> directly from <code>data.js</code>. The two systems were never reconciled — that's how #1 slipped through.</p>
      <p><strong>Verdict:</strong> confirmed.</p>

      <h3>#9 — <code>getTotalCartAmount</code> briefly returns <code>$0</code></h3>
      <pre><code>// front/src/context/ShopContext.jsx
const getTotalCartAmount = () => {
  return Object.entries(cartItems).reduce((total, [id, qty]) => {
    const product = all_products.find((p) =&gt; p._id === id)
    return total + (product ? product.price * qty : 0)
  }, 0)
}</code></pre>
      <p>On page load, <code>all_products</code> is <code>[]</code> until the fetch resolves. During that window, every lookup returns <code>undefined</code>, the guard collapses to <code>0</code>, and the total is silently <code>$0</code> even for a full cart.</p>
      <p><strong>Verdict:</strong> confirmed. The guard prevents NaN, but the transient <code>$0</code> is a real UX bug.</p>

      <h3>#10 — Orphaned cart keys after product deletion</h3>
      <p>The current <code>getTotalCartAmount</code> <em>does</em> guard with <code>product ? ... : 0</code>, so NaN doesn't occur — the brief's description is slightly stronger than reality. But the orphaned key still lives in <code>cartItems</code> forever, and the legacy <code>Cart.jsx</code> silently filters it out. That means a user can see a cart line disappear without explanation.</p>
      <p><strong>Verdict:</strong> partially confirmed — no NaN, but still orphaned-key state.</p>

      <h3>#11 — <code>removeFromCart</code> ignores backend failure</h3>
      <pre><code>const removeFromCart = async (id, removeAll = false) =&gt; {
  setCartItems((prev) =&gt; { /* optimistic update */ });
  if (token) {
    try {
      await axios.post(`${API_URL}/api/cart/remove`, { id }, { headers: { token } });
    } catch (err) {
      console.log("Cart remove error:", err);   // ← swallowed
    }
  }
}</code></pre>
      <p><strong>Verdict:</strong> confirmed. Optimistic removal stays in the UI; the server keeps the item. Next page reload re-syncs from the backend and the item reappears — the user's click appears to have done nothing.</p>

      <h3>#12 — No JWT expiry handling</h3>
      <pre><code>// back/middleware/auth.js
try {
  const token_decode = jwt.verify(token, process.env.JWT_SECRET);
  req.userId = token_decode.id;
  next();
} catch (err) {
  res.json({ success: false, message: err.message });  // raw JWT error
}</code></pre>
      <p>The token lives 7 days. After expiry, <code>jwt.verify</code> throws <code>TokenExpiredError</code>, the middleware returns it verbatim, and no client code distinguishes expiry from “not logged in.” The user is stuck with a stale token in <code>localStorage</code> forever.</p>
      <p><strong>Verdict:</strong> confirmed.</p>

      <h3>#13 — No stock check at order time</h3>
      <p><code>placeOrder</code> reads <code>req.body.items</code>, builds a Stripe session, and persists the order — but <code>back/models/productModel.js</code> has no <code>stock</code> field at all. There is nothing to check.</p>
      <p><strong>Verdict:</strong> confirmed. Stock tracking has to be introduced as a new capability, not fixed as a bug.</p>

      <h3>#15 — No duplicate slug/name check on products</h3>
      <p><code>addProduct</code> inserts unconditionally. There is no unique index on <code>name</code> in the schema and no pre-insert query.</p>
      <p><strong>Verdict:</strong> confirmed.</p>

      <h3>#16 — Stripe flow has no webhook</h3>
      <pre><code>const session = await stripe.checkout.sessions.create({
  line_items,
  mode: "payment",
  success_url: `${frontend_url}/verify?success=true&amp;orderId=${newOrder._id}`,
  cancel_url:  `${frontend_url}/verify?success=false&amp;orderId=${newOrder._id}`,
});</code></pre>
      <p>Order state is driven by the browser hitting <code>/verify</code>. If the user closes the tab after paying, <code>payment: true</code> is never set. If the user manually visits <code>/verify?success=true&amp;orderId=xyz</code>, an unpaid order is marked paid.</p>
      <p><strong>Verdict:</strong> confirmed. Correct fix is a signature-verified webhook at <code>/api/webhooks/stripe</code> (Phase 6).</p>
    </section>

    <section id="extra">
      <h2><span class="num">6</span> Additional Findings — Beyond the Inventory</h2>
      <p>Two extra issues surfaced during the audit pass. Neither was in the original brief.</p>

      <h3>A — <code>userController.registerUser</code> trusts bcrypt in the wrong order</h3>
      <pre><code>const salt = await bcrypt.genSalt(10);
const hashedpassword = await bcrypt.hash(password, salt);</code></pre>
      <p>This works, but it's duplicated in <code>adminController.setupFirstAdmin</code> with the same code. When the app moves to Next.js, this pattern collapses into one <code>hashPassword()</code> helper — otherwise password policies drift between the two call sites. Recorded for Phase 3.</p>

      <h3>B — <code>adminController.adminLogin</code> leaks whether an email exists</h3>
      <table>
        <thead><tr><th>Case</th><th>Response</th></tr></thead>
        <tbody>
          <tr><td>Email not found</td><td><code>{ success: false, message: "User Not Found" }</code></td></tr>
          <tr><td>Email exists, not admin</td><td><code>{ success: false, message: "User Not an Admin" }</code></td></tr>
          <tr><td>Email exists, admin, wrong password</td><td><code>{ success: false, message: "Invalid Password" }</code></td></tr>
        </tbody>
      </table>
      <p>Three distinct messages → an attacker can enumerate valid emails and privileged accounts by reading the response text. The Phase 3 fix is the standard pattern: one generic error for all failure modes.</p>
      <div class="callout success">
        <strong>Not in the original inventory</strong>
        Fixing this in the new build is not “scope creep” — it's a free improvement because the login flow is being rewritten anyway.
      </div>
    </section>

    <section id="decision">
      <h2><span class="num">7</span> Architectural Decisions</h2>

      <h3>7.1 — A new sibling folder, not a rename</h3>
      <p><code>shop/</code> sits next to <code>front/</code>, <code>back/</code>, and <code>admin/</code>. Nothing in the legacy trees is modified. The reference implementation stays runnable until the new app fully replaces it.</p>
      <table>
        <thead><tr><th>Alternative</th><th>Rejected because</th></tr></thead>
        <tbody>
          <tr><td>Rename <code>front/</code> → <code>shop/</code></td><td>Destroys the reference; forces a hard cutover mid-project</td></tr>
          <tr><td>Monorepo with workspaces</td><td>Adds complexity with zero payoff for a single-app rewrite</td></tr>
          <tr><td>Subfolder of the legacy repo</td><td>Mixes histories; git blame becomes unusable</td></tr>
        </tbody>
      </table>

      <h3>7.2 — Fresh git repository</h3>
      <p><code>shop/</code> gets its own <code>.git</code>. The legacy repo's history includes committed <code>.env</code> files (#7) — separating the histories means those secrets never appear in the new repo's blame, logs, or commit graph.</p>

      <h3>7.3 — Neon from day one (no SQLite stopover)</h3>
      <p>The earlier Lumière build started on SQLite and migrated later. That migration produced five distinct deployment errors — the pattern is well understood now, and there is nothing to gain from repeating it. Using Neon from Phase 1 means Phase 1's <code>schema.prisma</code> is identical to Phase 10's, minus the models.</p>

      <h3>7.4 — Webpack, not Turbopack</h3>
      <p><code>PrismaPlugin</code> is a webpack plugin. Any project that uses it must build with Webpack. Rather than fight this later, the <code>--webpack</code> flag is added to both <code>dev</code> and <code>build</code> in Phase 1's <code>package.json</code> — this is the same decision made after five errors on Lumière, now applied preemptively.</p>
    </section>

    <section id="stack">
      <h2><span class="num">8</span> Stack &amp; Tooling</h2>
      <table>
        <thead><tr><th>Layer</th><th>Choice</th><th>Why this, not the alternative</th></tr></thead>
        <tbody>
          <tr><td>Framework</td><td>Next.js 16 (App Router)</td><td>Proven in the Lumière build; single codebase replaces <code>front/</code> + <code>admin/</code> + <code>back/</code></td></tr>
          <tr><td>Language</td><td>TypeScript 5</td><td>End-to-end type safety from Prisma → services → UI</td></tr>
          <tr><td>Database</td><td>Neon PostgreSQL (from day one)</td><td>Serverless Postgres; avoids the SQLite → Postgres migration the Lumière build paid for</td></tr>
          <tr><td>ORM</td><td>Prisma 6 (<code>prisma-client-js</code>)</td><td><code>prisma-client</code> generator fails to bundle the query engine on Vercel — verified in Lumière Phase 9</td></tr>
          <tr><td>Styling</td><td>Tailwind CSS 4</td><td>Same version as Lumière; zero-dependency utility CSS</td></tr>
          <tr><td>Linting</td><td>ESLint 9 + <code>eslint-config-next</code></td><td>Default in <code>create-next-app</code>; the modern flat config</td></tr>
          <tr><td>Formatting</td><td>Prettier 3 + <code>prettier-plugin-tailwindcss</code></td><td>Deterministic class ordering, zero bikeshedding</td></tr>
          <tr><td>Git hooks</td><td>Husky 9 + lint-staged 15</td><td>Pre-commit lint + format on changed files only</td></tr>
          <tr><td>TypeScript runner</td><td>tsx</td><td>Required for the <code>predev</code>/<code>prebuild</code> image-generation script</td></tr>
        </tbody>
      </table>
      <div class="callout info">
        <strong>Deferred to later phases</strong>
        Auth.js v5 (Phase 3), Zod 4 (Phase 3), next-intl v4 (Phase 9), Stripe (Phase 6), Resend + React Email (Phase 9), Recharts (Phase 8), Vitest + Playwright (Phase 10). Installing them in Phase 1 would ship unused code.
      </div>
    </section>

    <section id="scaffold">
      <h2><span class="num">9</span> Scaffolding Steps</h2>
      <p>Full step list lives in the phase's companion document. The high-level order:</p>
      <ol>
        <li><code>npx create-next-app@latest shop</code> from the parent directory — TypeScript, Tailwind, <code>src/</code>, App Router, no Turbopack.</li>
        <li>Pin Prisma to 6.x if the scaffolder pulled an RC (the Lumière gotcha).</li>
        <li>Install supporting tooling: Prettier, Husky, lint-staged, tsx, dotenv, <code>@prisma/nextjs-monorepo-workaround-plugin</code>.</li>
        <li><code>npx prisma init --datasource-provider postgresql</code>, then replace the generated schema with the Phase-1 skeleton.</li>
        <li>Write <code>prisma.config.ts</code> with a CI-safe fallback URL.</li>
        <li>Add <code>src/lib/prisma.ts</code> — hot-reload-safe singleton.</li>
        <li>Wire <code>PrismaPlugin</code> into <code>next.config.ts</code>.</li>
        <li>Add <code>scripts/generate-local-images.ts</code> and its <code>predev</code>/<code>prebuild</code> hooks.</li>
        <li>Add <code>--webpack</code> to <code>dev</code> and <code>build</code>.</li>
        <li>Husky + lint-staged wired to a pre-commit hook.</li>
        <li>Extend <code>.gitignore</code>; create <code>.env</code> and <code>.env.example</code>.</li>
        <li>Green build, silent typecheck, initial commit.</li>
      </ol>
    </section>

    <section id="structure">
      <h2><span class="num">10</span> Folder Structure (after Phase 1)</h2>
      <div class="filetree">

      <p>Phase 2 adds all models to <code>schema.prisma</code> and runs the first migration. Phase 3 adds <code>src/auth.ts</code>, <code>src/auth.config.ts</code>, and the <code>(auth)</code> route group. Phase 4 adds <code>(shop)/</code>. Nothing here is speculative — every folder exists because a specific phase will fill it.</p>
    </section>

    <section id="config">
      <h2><span class="num">11</span> Key Config Files (Highlights)</h2>

      <h3>schema.prisma — Phase 1 skeleton</h3>
      <pre><code>generator client {
  provider      = "prisma-client-js"
  binaryTargets = ["native", "rhel-openssl-3.0.x"]
}

datasource db {
  provider  = "postgresql"
  url       = env("DATABASE_URL")
  directUrl = env("DIRECT_URL")
}</code></pre>
      <p>Two deliberate choices: <code>prisma-client-js</code> (not <code>prisma-client</code>) and the RHEL binary target. Both were learned the hard way in Lumière Phase 9.</p>

      <h3>package.json — scripts</h3>
      <pre><code>"predev":     "tsx scripts/generate-local-images.ts",
"prebuild":   "tsx scripts/generate-local-images.ts",
"dev":        "next dev --webpack",
"build":      "next build --webpack",
"postinstall": "prisma generate",
"prepare":    "husky"</code></pre>
      <p>Every one of these lines maps to a specific failure mode paid for on the previous project.</p>

      <h3>next.config.ts — PrismaPlugin</h3>
      <pre><code>webpack: (config, { isServer }) =&gt; {
  if (isServer) {
    config.plugins = [...config.plugins, new PrismaPlugin()];
  }
  return config;
}</code></pre>
      <p>Server-only — the client bundle has no business touching Prisma.</p>
    </section>

    <section id="gotchas">
      <h2><span class="num">12</span> Preempted Gotchas</h2>
      <p>These are the exact five production errors the Lumière build hit after its first deploy, now baked into Phase 1 so they never fire on <code>shop/</code>.</p>
      <table>
        <thead><tr><th>#</th><th>Lum&egrave;re error</th><th>Phase 1 defence</th></tr></thead>
        <tbody>
          <tr><td>1</td><td><code>Can't reach database server</code> during build (DB-driven pages prerendered)</td><td>Every page that queries Prisma will carry <code>export const dynamic = "force-dynamic"</code>. Recorded here; applied from Phase 4 when the first such page exists.</td></tr>
          <tr><td>2</td><td>Missing TypeScript declaration for <code>@prisma/nextjs-monorepo-workaround-plugin</code></td><td>Add <code>src/types/prisma-plugin.d.ts</code> when the first <code>tsc</code> pass complains. Deferred to first actual typecheck run.</td></tr>
          <tr><td>3</td><td>Turbopack rejects the Webpack config</td><td><code>--webpack</code> in both <code>dev</code> and <code>build</code> from day one.</td></tr>
          <tr><td>4</td><td>Query engine missing on Vercel (<code>rhel-openssl-3.0.x</code>)</td><td><code>binaryTargets = ["native", "rhel-openssl-3.0.x"]</code> in the schema.</td></tr>
          <tr><td>5</td><td>Neon pooler rejects serverless connections</td><td><code>.env.example</code> documents the direct endpoint explicitly.</td></tr>
        </tbody>
      </table>
      <div class="callout warn">
        <strong>Two items are deliberately deferred</strong>
        #1 and #2 cannot be applied before the conditions that trigger them exist. They are pre-recorded so they don't get re-learned — but forcing them now would ship dead code.
      </div>
    </section>

    <section id="verify">

    <section id="summary">
      <h2><span class="num">14</span> Summary</h2>
      <h3>Audit — all 16 inventory items verified</h3>
      <ul>
        <li><strong>CRITICAL (3).</strong> Broken imports crash two public routes; admin order list is always empty; three files are dead placeholders.</li>
        <li><strong>SECURITY (4).</strong> Login bypass with hardcoded credentials; a protected-route key that nothing writes; a public admin-claim endpoint; committed <code>.env</code> files; unrestricted Multer uploads.</li>
        <li><strong>LOGIC (9).</strong> Two sources of truth; transient <code>$0</code> cart total; orphaned cart keys; ignored backend failure on cart mutations; no JWT expiry handling; no stock tracking; no duplicate-slug check; no Stripe webhook.</li>
        <li><strong>Additional findings (2).</strong> Duplicated bcrypt code paths, and a user-enumeration leak in <code>adminLogin</code> (three distinct error messages).</li>
      </ul>

      <h3>Scaffold — everything needed for Phase 2</h3>
      <ul>
        <li>Next.js 16 + TypeScript 5 + Tailwind 4, App Router, <code>src/</code>, no Turbopack.</li>
        <li>Prisma 6 pinned; schema with the RHEL binary target; <code>prisma.config.ts</code> with a CI-safe fallback.</li>
        <li><code>--webpack</code> on <code>dev</code> and <code>build</code>; <code>postinstall: prisma generate</code>.</li>
        <li><code>predev</code>/<code>prebuild</code> hooks calling the auto-generated image script.</li>
        <li>Prettier + ESLint + Husky + lint-staged — pre-commit hook active.</li>
        <li><code>src/lib/prisma.ts</code> — hot-reload-safe singleton.</li>
        <li>Initial commit <code>Phase 1: scaffold + audit</code>.</li>
      </ul>

      <h3>Engineering outcomes</h3>
      <ul>
        <li>Every bug from the brief is confirmed with file-level evidence, not assumed.</li>
        <li>The five Lumière deployment gotchas are pre-empted — three applied, two pre-recorded with the phase that triggers them.</li>
        <li>The legacy trees stay runnable and unmodified.</li>
        <li>Phase 2 can start with zero cleanup work: the only thing it will do is add models to <code>schema.prisma</code> and run the first migration.</li>
      </ul>

      <div class="callout info">
        <strong>Ready for Phase 2 when confirmed</strong>
        Phase 2 will define every model — User, Address, Category, Product, ProductVariant, ProductImage, CartItem, Order, OrderItem, Review, ReviewImage, Coupon, Wishlist, AuditLog, Setting — with relations, onDelete rules, and indexes. It will also seed 4 categories and 60 products with variants.
      </div>
    </section>

<file path="scripts/generate-local-images.ts">
// ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════
// 🖼️  Generate Local Images List
// ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════
// Reads public/products/ at BUILD time and writes a typed
// constant consumed by the admin image picker (Phase 8).
//
// Why build time: Vercel serves public/ from the CDN and
// the serverless runtime cannot read it at request time.

import { readdirSync, writeFileSync, existsSync, mkdirSync } from "node:fs";
import { join } from "node:path";

const PRODUCTS_DIR = join(process.cwd(), "public", "products");
const OUT_FILE = join(
  process.cwd(),
  "src",
  "lib",
  "constants",
  "local-images.generated.ts"
);

const ALLOWED_EXTENSIONS = new Set([
  ".jpg",
  ".jpeg",
  ".png",
  ".webp",
  ".avif",
  ".gif",
  ".svg",
]);

function main() {
  if (!existsSync(PRODUCTS_DIR)) {
    mkdirSync(PRODUCTS_DIR, { recursive: true });
  }

  const files = readdirSync(PRODUCTS_DIR)
    .filter((name) => {
      const dot = name.lastIndexOf(".");
      if (dot === -1) return false;
      return ALLOWED_EXTENSIONS.has(name.slice(dot).toLowerCase());
    })
    .sort();

  const lines = files.map((n) => `  "/products/${n}",`).join("\n");

  const content = `// ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════
// 🖼️  Local Images (AUTO-GENERATED — do not edit manually)
// ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════
// Generated by scripts/generate-local-images.ts
// Runs automatically before \`npm run dev\` and \`npm run build\`.
//
// To add new images: drop them in public/products/ and restart dev.

export const LOCAL_IMAGES = [
${lines}
] as const;

export type LocalImage = (typeof LOCAL_IMAGES)[number];
`;

  writeFileSync(OUT_FILE, content, "utf8");
  console.log(
    `✅ Generated ${files.length} product image reference(s) → src/lib/constants/local-images.generated.ts`
  );
}

main();
</file>

<file path="src/lib/prisma.ts">
// ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════
// 🗄️ Prisma Client singleton
// ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════
// Prevents connection-pool exhaustion during `next dev` HMR.
// In production, the module graph is only evaluated once,
// so the cached instance is a no-op.

import { PrismaClient } from "@prisma/client";

const globalForPrisma = globalThis as unknown as {
  prisma: PrismaClient | undefined;
};

export const prisma =
  globalForPrisma.prisma ??
  new PrismaClient({
    log: ["error", "warn"],
  });

if (process.env.NODE_ENV !== "production") {
  globalForPrisma.prisma = prisma;
}
</file>

<file path="prisma.config.ts">
// ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════
// ⚙️ Prisma 6 configuration
// ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════
// dotenv/config is required: Prisma 6 no longer auto-loads
// .env when using prisma.config.ts.
//
// The fallback URL prevents `prisma generate` from failing
// in CI where no real DATABASE_URL is provided.

import "dotenv/config";
import { defineConfig } from "prisma/config";

const FALLBACK_URL =
  "postgresql://placeholder:placeholder@localhost:5432/placeholder";

export default defineConfig({
  schema: "prisma/schema.prisma",
  migrations: {
    path: "prisma/migrations",
  },
  engine: "classic",
  datasource: {
    url: process.env.DATABASE_URL ?? FALLBACK_URL,
  },
});
</file>

<file path="prisma/schema.prisma">
// ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════
// 🛒 shop/ — Prisma schema
// ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════
// Phase 1 ships ONLY the generator + datasource.
// All models (User, Product, Order, etc.) land in Phase 2.
//
// Deployment notes (from the Lumière lessons):
//   • prisma-client-js — NOT the newer `prisma-client` generator.
//     Outputs to node_modules and is bundled correctly on Vercel.
//   • binaryTargets — native (dev) + rhel-openssl-3.0.x (Vercel).
//   • DATABASE_URL is the runtime connection (direct endpoint on Neon).
//   • DIRECT_URL is used only by `prisma migrate`.

generator client {
  provider      = "prisma-client-js"
  binaryTargets = ["native", "rhel-openssl-3.0.x"]
}

datasource db {
  provider  = "postgresql"
  url       = env("DATABASE_URL")
  directUrl = env("DIRECT_URL")
}
</file>

<file path="public/products/.gitkeep">

</file>

<file path="scripts/generate-local-images.ts">
// ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════
// 🖼️  Generate Local Images List
// ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════
// Reads public/products/ at BUILD time and writes a typed
// constant consumed by the admin image picker (Phase 8).
//
// Why build time: Vercel serves public/ from the CDN and
// the serverless runtime cannot read it at request time.

import { readdirSync, writeFileSync, existsSync, mkdirSync } from "node:fs";
import { join } from "node:path";

const PRODUCTS_DIR = join(process.cwd(), "public", "products");
const OUT_FILE = join(
  process.cwd(),
  "src",
  "lib",
  "constants",
  "local-images.generated.ts"
);

const ALLOWED_EXTENSIONS = new Set([
  ".jpg",
  ".jpeg",
  ".png",
  ".webp",
  ".avif",
  ".gif",
  ".svg",
]);

function main() {
  if (!existsSync(PRODUCTS_DIR)) {
    mkdirSync(PRODUCTS_DIR, { recursive: true });
  }

  const files = readdirSync(PRODUCTS_DIR)
    .filter((name) => {
      const dot = name.lastIndexOf(".");
      if (dot === -1) return false;
      return ALLOWED_EXTENSIONS.has(name.slice(dot).toLowerCase());
    })
    .sort();

  const lines = files.map((n) => `  "/products/${n}",`).join("\n");

  const content = `// ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════
// 🖼️  Local Images (AUTO-GENERATED — do not edit manually)
// ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════
// Generated by scripts/generate-local-images.ts
// Runs automatically before \`npm run dev\` and \`npm run build\`.
//
// To add new images: drop them in public/products/ and restart dev.

export const LOCAL_IMAGES = [
${lines}
] as const;

export type LocalImage = (typeof LOCAL_IMAGES)[number];
`;

  writeFileSync(OUT_FILE, content, "utf8");
  console.log(
    `✅ Generated ${files.length} product image reference(s) → src/lib/constants/local-images.generated.ts`
  );
}

main();
</file>

<file path="src/lib/prisma.ts">
// ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════
// 🗄️ Prisma Client singleton
// ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════
// Prevents connection-pool exhaustion during `next dev` HMR.
// In production, the module graph is only evaluated once,
// so the cached instance is a no-op.

import { PrismaClient } from "@prisma/client";

const globalForPrisma = globalThis as unknown as {
  prisma: PrismaClient | undefined;
};

export const prisma =
  globalForPrisma.prisma ??
  new PrismaClient({
    log: ["error", "warn"],
  });

if (process.env.NODE_ENV !== "production") {
  globalForPrisma.prisma = prisma;
}
</file>

// ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════
// ⚙️ Prisma 6 configuration
// ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════
// dotenv/config is required: Prisma 6 no longer auto-loads
// .env when using prisma.config.ts.
//
// The fallback URL prevents `prisma generate` from failing
// in CI where no real DATABASE_URL is provided.

import "dotenv/config";
import { defineConfig } from "prisma/config";

const FALLBACK_URL =
  "postgresql://placeholder:placeholder@localhost:5432/placeholder";

export default defineConfig({
  schema: "prisma/schema.prisma",
  migrations: {
    path: "prisma/migrations",
  },
  engine: "classic",
  datasource: {
    url: process.env.DATABASE_URL ?? FALLBACK_URL,
  },
});

<file path="next.config.ts">
import type { NextConfig } from "next";
import { PrismaPlugin } from "@prisma/nextjs-monorepo-workaround-plugin";

const nextConfig: NextConfig = {
  // PrismaPlugin must be applied to the server bundle only.
  // Requires Webpack — hence the `--webpack` flags in package.json.
  webpack: (config, { isServer }) => {
    if (isServer) {
      config.plugins = [...config.plugins, new PrismaPlugin()];
    }
    return config;
  },

  // Remote image hosts used by later phases (Unsplash hero,
  // flag CDN for the language switcher in Phase 9).
  images: {
    remotePatterns: [
      { protocol: "https", hostname: "images.unsplash.com" },
      { protocol: "https", hostname: "flagcdn.com" },
    ],
  },
};

export default nextConfig;
</file>

<file path="README.md">
# e-shop/

A Next.js 16 e-commerce app — the production rewrite of a legacy MERN
storefront (kept in `../front`, `../admin`, `../back` as reference).

**Status:** Phase 1 complete — scaffold + audit.

## Stack

Next.js 16 (App Router) · TypeScript · Prisma 6 · Neon PostgreSQL ·
Tailwind CSS 4 · Vercel

## Getting started

```bash
cp .env.example .env      # fill in Neon DATABASE_URL + DIRECT_URL
npm install
npm run dev
</file>

import type { Metadata } from "next";
import { Geist, Geist_Mono } from "next/font/google";
import "./globals.css";

const geistSans = Geist({
  variable: "--font-geist-sans",
  subsets: ["latin"],
});

const geistMono = Geist_Mono({
  variable: "--font-geist-mono",
  subsets: ["latin"],
});

export const metadata: Metadata = {
  title: "Create Next App",
  description: "Generated by create next app",
};

export default function RootLayout({ children }: LayoutProps<"/">) {
  return (
    <html
      lang="en"
      className={`${geistSans.variable} ${geistMono.variable} h-full antialiased`}
    >
      <body className="min-h-full flex flex-col">{children}</body>
    </html>
  );
}
</file>

<file path="next.config.ts">
import type { NextConfig } from "next";
import { PrismaPlugin } from "@prisma/nextjs-monorepo-workaround-plugin";

const nextConfig: NextConfig = {
  // PrismaPlugin must be applied to the server bundle only.
  // Requires Webpack — hence the `--webpack` flags in package.json.
  webpack: (config, { isServer }) => {
    if (isServer) {
      config.plugins = [...config.plugins, new PrismaPlugin()];
    }
    return config;
  },

  // Remote image hosts used by later phases (Unsplash hero,
  // flag CDN for the language switcher in Phase 9).
  images: {
    remotePatterns: [
      { protocol: "https", hostname: "images.unsplash.com" },
      { protocol: "https", hostname: "flagcdn.com" },
    ],
  },
};

export default nextConfig;
</file>

<file path="README.md">
# e-shop/

A Next.js 16 e-commerce app — the production rewrite of a legacy MERN
storefront (kept in `../front`, `../admin`, `../back` as reference).

**Status:** Phase 1 complete — scaffold + audit.

## Stack

Next.js 16 (App Router) · TypeScript · Prisma 6 · Neon PostgreSQL ·
Tailwind CSS 4 · Vercel

## Getting started

```bash
cp .env.example .env      # fill in Neon DATABASE_URL + DIRECT_URL
npm install
npm run dev
</file>
